newsitem.title: USA: GE says it is well positioned for 1997.
newsitem.headline: GE says it is well positioned for 1997.

text.p: General Electric Co said it was in a position to deliver a record performance in 1997 following strong results in the first quarter.

GE reported record first-quarter earnings of $1.02 a share, up 12 percent from last year. GE's first-quarter operating margin increased to 14.3 percent of sales, up from last year's 13.7 percent, and also was a record for the quarter.

"The record results once again demonstrate how GE, with its mix of leading global businesses, can consistently deliver top-line growth, increased margins and strong cash generation," chairman John Welch said.
The results were led by strong double-digit increases in Specialized Financing, Specialty Insurance and Equipment Management activities.
Cash generated from GE's operating activities was $1.3 billion in the first quarter, up from last year's $1.2 billion.
As part of the $13 billion share repurchase program, GE purchased $843 million of its stock during the first quarter to reach $7.3 billion.
"During the quarter, GE's expansion into services accelerated," Welch said.
GE said NBC won its ninth consecutive ratings sweep and moved its MSNBC operations into a new state-of-the-art studio.
GE Capital continued its insurance growth with the acquisition of Coregis, Xerox's property and casualty insurance business.
GE Information Services expanded its internet activities with a joint venture with Thomas Publishing and a new venture with Netscape.
The equipment service businesses continued their rapid expansion as Power Systems closed long-term service agreements valued at $700 million, GE said.
Aircraft Engines announced an agreement to acquire Greenwich Air Services and UNC Incorporated, with joint revenues of $1.8 billion, to expand its service capabilities.
Aircraft Engines also continued its strong performance by winning more than 60 percent of the orders for large commercial engines during the quarter.
Recent Delta Air Lines' orders alone totaled $1.3 billion for engines to power 101 Boeing 737 and 767 aircraft, GE said.
